title: CopperGate QSR onboarding scratch notes
content:
SUMMARY: Notes from kickoff + deep-dive with CopperGate (fast-casual/QSR POS vendor). They want a low-latency voice upsell assistant for drive-thru and pickup kiosks. Primary asks: ~100ms extra latency budget per request, 99.9% uptime, private deployment (VPC/air-gapped option for some enterprise customers), and PCI-scope minimization.

2025-01-09 call (60m) attendees: CopperGate — Lina Park (CTO), Marco Ruiz (Platform), Aisha Khan (Product); Redwood — Priya (SE), Ethan (Infra lead), Sofia (Security).

Key customer goals:
- Drive-thru voice assistant: short prompts, incremental streaming output to TTS; must be <250ms RTT ideally, but CopperGate comfortable with up to 350ms in practice given network hops.
- On-device/edge adapters: PoC needs to integrate with existing POS edge gateways (ARM x86 mixed fleet) — prefer a hybrid model: inference in regional private cluster + small edge cache for fallbacks.
- Data residency & PCI: customer will not send full card PANs to Redwood; any token / receipt data must be redacted client-side. They request integration with their KMS (HashiCorp Vault) and ability to use an HSM in dedicated private deployment.
- Model governance: need pinning to a model version, ability to rollback on quality regressions, and simple canary rollout across regions.

Technical constraints & gotchas observed:
- Network egress: some franchise locations have asymmetric links with high jitter; we should recommend using persistent connections (HTTP/2 or gRPC) and enable request-level RTT metrics in the agent.
- TTS streaming: CopperGate uses a homegrown TTS with 60ms buffer; Redwood streaming chunk sizes and chunk timing will need tuning to avoid audible gaps. Long-form streaming causes buffer starvation at lower bitrates.
- KV/prefix caching: drive-thru conversations often repeat menu prompts. Suggest enabling prefix caching and a small local cache layer on gateways to reduce tokens for repeated prompts. Document expected cache hit/miss behavior for EMR (menu changes during promos).
- Model size vs latency: recommend 7B quantized variant for regional clusters to meet latency SLO; fall back to smaller distilled 3B for ultra-low-latency kiosks. Need to validate quality regression with eval set (we proposed a 2000-sample prompt eval covering promos, combos, and customer accent variations).
- Autoscaling: peak times (lunch/dinner) have bursty patterns. Dedicated capacity with fast-scalers required; autoscaling cooldowns need to avoid cold-start latency spikes.

Open questions (must confirm):
1) Which franchises require on-prem air-gapped option vs VPC-only? (Lina to follow up with list by 2025-01-16)
2) POS gateway hardware inventory (ARM/Intel/Memory/RAM/disk) — Marco to share CSV.
3) What are their exact TTS chunking parameters and audio codec? We need sample WAV/OPUS to test streaming glue.
4) Legal: what metadata will be logged? They prefer minimal request/response logging; need to confirm retention window.

Immediate next steps & owners:
- SE: create a short PoC plan doc (3-week) with milestones: infra template, sample model selection, eval harness, end-to-end latency test — owner: Priya — target 2025-01-17 (Jira CUST-342 linked).
- Infra: prepare a Dedicated-region template (us-west-2) with Vault/KMS integration + HSM stub for dev — owner: Ethan — target 2025-01-20.
- Security: draft logging/dataflow diagram and retention recommendations for CopperGate legal — owner: Sofia — target 2025-01-16.
- Product: prepare canary rollout config options (traffic split, automatic rollback triggers) and discuss with Marco — owner: Jamal — target 2025-01-21.
- Engineering: create a streaming TTS test harness (client and server side) and run with sample OPUS file from CopperGate — owner: eng-sre pair (TBD) — target 2025-01-24.

Notes to self / assumptions to validate:
- We'll assume CopperGate will run PBX/edge gateway clients that can maintain 2 persistent streams per device. If fewer, our batching/caching recommendations change.
- For initial PoC use: quantized 7B (GPT-like) + prompt engineering to keep token counts low. Budget estimate for PoC: ~1-2k tokens/session * avg 300 sessions/day across 50 stores (config to be refined).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: quality drop when using 3B fallback. Mitigate: automated eval on their accent dataset; keep canary threshold conservative.
- Risk: cold-start latency during promos. Mitigate: pre-warm policy for predicted peak windows, and short warm-latency reserve capacity.

Meeting artifacts & links:
- Engagement ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CUST-342
- Initial PR with PoC infra template (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/recipes/pull/478
- Slack thread: #SE-coppergate-thread (internal)

Random UX thoughts captured mid-call:
- Offer a thin SDK for their edge gateway that exposes a streaming API and automatic reconnect/backoff; allow offline fallback to canned responses for 5–10 seconds to keep UX from stalling.
- Consider tagging menu updates as short-lived keys in prefix cache so promotions expire automatically.

Action log (short):
- 2025-01-10: Priya wrote draft PoC plan (attach later).
- 2025-01-11: Ethan spun up dev cluster template, awaiting Vault credentials from customer.
- 2025-01-14: Sofia sent initial logging recommendations to Lina.

- Add sample OPUS file under linked artifacts once CopperGate shares.
- Draft short customer-facing one-pager summarizing PoC scope and success criteria (Priya).
